verdicts.claim: Civilian deaths give no benefit and the villain never feeds on them, yet menace on main and the live pin is fed by casualties (0.9 a person) and gives ki regen, up to +5% damage and beam power.
verdicts.what_is_true: At HEAD and the live pin, WorldCollateral._feed adds 0.9 menace per casualty to a fighter with menace, and also 0.09 power per casualty (hard-coded, collateral.gd:358), which earns tiers (fighter.gd:555). Menace gives ki regen, up to +5% damage and beam power. This breaks Orb's pillar 5 (vision.md:1585) and c08 as RL-217 sharpened it. Feeding on evacuees fits Orb's 'mass evacuation' wording. The school and children parts hold: no child exists in the data, and the chapel is barred at HEAD (AC-172).
external: https://pegi.info/what-do-the-labels-mean (accessed 2026-11-07): PEGI 18 covers "violence towards defenceless characters"
verdicts.fix: Game Design moves menace's casualty source to non-lethal inputs and deletes the casualty-to-power line. Until that lands, the Steam content survey must say the villain gains from civilian deaths. Retire the older records that contradict the rule.
verdicts.belongs_to: Game Design (fix); Legal (ratings); Orb's creative direction (pillar 5)

verdicts.claim: Answer the Steam content survey and IARC early and honestly from the real build, with matching descriptors, and never promise a rating; Orb targets Mature while Legal predicts Teen or PEGI 12-16.
verdicts.what_is_true: The repo holds no survey or IARC answers, and the records disagree: vision.md:63 targets Mature, the store draft says cartoon violence, and the uncommitted RL-247 predicts Teen. Valve's Germany page confirms the 2024-11-15 rule and that Valve's own rating needs the content survey. steam-readiness.md:44 wrongly calls IARC 'for itch.io', while go-to-market.md:150 says itch.io needs no rating.
external: https://partner.steamgames.com/doc/gettingstarted/contentsurvey/germany (accessed 2026-11-07): "Steam will no longer display games to customers in Germany"
verdicts.fix: Before any store page, Legal runs the content survey on the real build and saves the answers, covering the menace gain and the civilian count. Correct steam-readiness.md:44 and align the store copy with the answers.

verdicts.claim: 1,800 civilians and the CIVILIANS LOST count pass in game, with a rule never to show the count above zero in public (w02).
verdicts.what_is_true: pop0 is 1,800, and the live /play/ build shows 'Civilians lost: n of 1800' on the pause screen and the results card. hud.gd:66 draws its line only in the F2 legacy HUD. w02 was withdrawn on 2026-10-12 (RL-132 and the withdrawn list), so the record's rule is not in force. Whether to show a count at all is Orb's call ("no death counters", vision.md:1585), which waits on the RL-247 hold.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: The row keeps a withdrawn public-screenshot rule marked Open, while nobody flags that the live count conflicts with Orb's later 'no death counters' direction.
verdicts.fix: Correct RL-129: w02 is withdrawn, and the amendment pasted on it is generic. After Orb's RL-247 follow-up, send removing the count to UI. Survey honesty stays under AC-170.

verdicts.claim: People terms in the launch planner are grandfathered; hill_chapel leaves every target list on main (noTarget plus filter), bell_tower becomes clock_tower, and the ratings answer says the villain AI prefers populated landings.
verdicts.what_is_true: At HEAD hill_chapel has noTarget, and launch, swing, arc and brunt all skip it; bell_tower is renamed clock_tower. The live pin keeps bell_tower and a chapel that can still be targeted, as RL-214 itself chose. launch.gd still reads popNear and popAlive at both commits. RL-214's status, 'Open until main's filter lands', is stale. clock_tower also has a duplicate hp_mult key.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: n/a (confirmed); the stale Open status keeps finished work on Legal's list.
verdicts.fix: Legal closes RL-214's filter condition. Put 'villain AI prefers populated landings' in the survey answers (AC-170). World removes the duplicate hp_mult.

verdicts.claim: RL-247 (uncommitted): Orb's bystander-comedy decisions sit under a HOLD until Orb's follow-up; predicted ESRB Teen, PEGI 12, USK 12.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-247 exists only in the uncommitted working copy, next to the untracked bystander-comedy-screen.md, yet committed rows (HEAD :463, :465) cite 'the RL-247 hold'. At HEAD, RL-248 to RL-255 sit after the Sources section. Orb's 2026-11-02 bystander decisions are not in vision.md. The predicted tiers cite no board source.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A hold that nobody can read in the public repo blocks bystander, toll and UI work, and committed rulings depend on it. The predicted tiers could be quoted as settled.
verdicts.fix: The EP commits RL-247 and its screen, moves the rows back inside the table, and records Orb's decisions in vision.md. Label the tiers as predictions until the survey result replaces them.

verdicts.claim: Civilian and hazard hard tests H1, H2 and H5 stay PENDING until LD1 and World's work land.
verdicts.what_is_true: pending-tests.js defines H1, H2 and H5. H4 and H5 have no body (run: null), and a test whose events are missing is reported PENDING. A hazard_telegraph event now exists (fx.gd:632) and matches the 'hazard*' prefix, so H1 and H2 may already run; I did not run them. They test casualty budgets and tier escalation, which is a design target (the P3 exit), not harm to players.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Carrying balance tests as safety gates makes the civilian share look like a release blocker and spends QA time under a safety label.
verdicts.fix: Move these to QA & Balance's design gates, write H5's body, and check whether H1 and H2 now run.

verdicts.claim: Blows to a downed opponent's head, face, neck or groin (s09) stay out of the base moveset until the rating decision; pins vertical, no choke or ground mount, holds time-limited.
verdicts.what_is_true: s09 and g07 keep blows to a downed opponent's head, chokes and ground mounts out of the moveset, and no such blow appears in the HEAD data. PEGI's basis is real: PEGI 18 names violence towards defenceless characters, though as an age-level criterion, not 'its own descriptor' as s09 says. It is a margin rule on content not yet built.
external: https://pegi.info/what-do-the-labels-mean (accessed 2026-11-07): PEGI 18 covers "violence towards defenceless characters"
verdicts.fix: Keep it as a design margin, correct the 'own descriptor' wording, and settle it once the survey (AC-170) is run.

verdicts.claim: The Cyborg is a predator of fighters: brief bite or clamp cleared; chewing, swallowing, gore and shown consumption off-screen; no eating finisher before the rating decision; never targets civilians or children.
verdicts.what_is_true: The Cyborg is not built (the roster holds PROTAGONIST, RIVAL and REFERENCE), so RL-220 guards future content. But finishers.json at HEAD and at the pin still names a 'devour finisher (graphic, Mature rating)' for him, which contradicts RL-220. That is public data, not shipped behaviour. The Teen and PEGI 12-16 predictions have no board source, while the catastrophe screen sets a Mature target.
verdicts.fix: Combat rewrites the Cyborg entry in finishers.json to RL-220's limits. The survey output replaces the predicted tiers.

verdicts.claim: The 2026-10-06 rule against showing buildings falling was withdrawn on 2026-10-12 as an over-literal reading of Orb's sarcasm; originality, truthful claims, AI disclosure, photosensitivity, p01 and p02 stand.
verdicts.what_is_true: RL-132 and movegen-banned.json's withdrawn list record the withdrawal, and vision.md:943-948 quotes Orb. The same amendment text is pasted on RL-124, RL-127, RL-128 and RL-129. The withdrawn rule was never a safety rule, and the rules that stand are tracked elsewhere. I did not check that every dependent ruling was re-made.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: It keeps an invented rule that was never about safety in the safety log. The pasted amendment misdescribes RL-129, whose guard was a public-count rule, not wording about towers.
verdicts.fix: Keep it as a process lesson, correct RL-129's amendment text, and gate nothing on it.

verdicts.claim: The 12-30% civilian band is re-based on places reached by a rule fixed in data (9,000 reach); whole-planet total reported, never a design input, reach changes go to Legal.
verdicts.what_is_true: farReach 9000 is in field.json:21, but plans.placesReached and WorldCollateral.placesReached are not on main: they exist only in docs, the parked places-reached diff and an optional read in records.gd. The band is a balance band that Legal itself says is never a target.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Treating a balance band and an unlanded denominator as safety rulings sends every reach change back to Legal and implies the band protects players.
verdicts.fix: Move the band to QA & Balance and Game Design. Correct RL-245's 'written in data' until the park lands.

verdicts.claim: Generated place names exclude real towns over 15,000 (eleven blocklisted, w06); no destroyed place named after a real city; no school, hospital or worship at any home; mushroom clouds avoid nuclear words (lint); mines never lasting hazards.
verdicts.what_is_true: The eleven names exist only in docs (narrative pending, world scratch). No place name and no blocklist_start is in the shipped data, so nothing ships today. c10's block words are in line-lint.json, but the lint is not wired into CI. The counts of 1,569 and 11 have no saved query. Sharing a name with a real town is a sensitivity margin, not a legal bar. I did not check mines (e13).
verdicts.fix: Land the blocklist together with the names, add the line lint to CI's data job once CI is repaired, and save the GeoNames query.

verdicts.claim: Pass-Through (civilians become food) is CONDITIONAL; store and mobile ratings unchecked; its replacement Press is GO with two conditions.
verdicts.what_is_true: q3-screen.md sets Pass-Through's conditions on franchise-echo grounds, and lines 110 and 136 replace it with Press (GO), yet RL-027 is still Open and on the P0 open-flag list. Neither is built. Orb's later lore lock (vision.md:1585, RL-220) has the Cyborg ignore civilians. The ratings note is the general survey duty (AC-170), and mobile is parked.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: A stale, Open P0 flag keeps a dead design on the gate list.
verdicts.fix: Close RL-027 as superseded and keep originality under Legal's IP screen.

verdicts.claim: Blood-heat power stage GO with conditions (limbs, veins, steam; never red or gold; no hair or eye change); mobile ratings unchecked.
verdicts.what_is_true: The conditions avoid franchise echoes (no red or gold, no hair or eye change), and the stage's look is not built: the data holds only heat numbers (styles.json:248). The mobile rating question is moot while mobile is parked (ADR 0011), and desktop ratings sit under AC-170.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: Small: one extra 'unchecked ratings' item for a parked platform.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Art and Legal's originality screen and drop the mobile item.

verdicts.claim: Vicious blows: s08 applies (arm as three places, two per place); vicious blows confirmed inside the clinch; launch pair has no bite, gouge or claw; rating question open for the Cyborg.
verdicts.what_is_true: s08 extends s02 to clinch taps, and s02's stated basis is a franchise echo ('keeps Blow for Blow ours'). Vicious blows are not built ('Not in G1', grapple.gd:30). The Cyborg rating question repeats AC-170 and AC-176.
verdicts.cost_of_false_alarm: An Open row, on originality grounds, waits for poses that do not exist.
verdicts.fix: Move it to Combat's originality checklist and fold the Cyborg ratings item into AC-170.

verdicts.claim: Swing toward towns: no swing score term reads people, arrivals are structures, terrain or fighters, no reward or text makes people the goal, camera never holds on civilians, band is a test result.
verdicts.what_is_true: At HEAD swing.gd reads no people term, and swing_legal_check.gd bars people words and tests that the scores ignore population. The swing is not in the live pin. The check is not wired into CI or any gate, and the swing can take an arrival picked by the launch planner, which does read people. I did not check the camera condition.
verdicts.fix: Wire swing_legal_check into the gates once CI is repaired, and update RL-213's status.
